newsitem.title: HAITI: Preval asks for extension of U.N. mandate in Haiti.
newsitem.headline: Preval asks for extension of U.N. mandate in Haiti.

text.p: Haiti asked for an eight-month extension of the United Nations peacekeeping mandate about two weeks before the troops were supposed to leave, President Rene Preval said on Wednesday.
Preval announced the request in answer to reporters' questions at the airport in Port-au-Prince before his departure on a one-week trip to Rome.

It was the third time Preval had asked for an extension of the mission. He and U.N. officials say an extension is needed while the Haitian National Police gain enough experience to maintain order in the country.
The police force was formed by international police trainers to replace the Haitian army, disbanded by former President Jean-Bertrand Aristide in 1995.

Observers say it will be easier for Preval's request to be approved in the U.N. security council as Haiti has improved diplomatic relations with China, which has previously opposed extending the mandate in Haiti.

The peacekeepers, some 1,600 of whom remain in Haiti, took over security responsibilities from 20,000 U.S. troops who restored Aristide to power in October 1994, three years after he was ousted in a bloody military coup.
